questions.question: What interaction constitutes an ionic bond?
questions.expected_answer: Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

questions.question: Why is describing an ionic bond only as an electron-transfer event incomplete?
questions.expected_answer: Electron transfer can create the ions, but the bond itself is the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

questions.question: What happens to electrons in a covalent bond?
questions.expected_answer: A pair of electrons is shared between atoms.

questions.question: A particle diagram shows two atoms associated with the same pair of electrons. Which bonding description fits this diagram, and why?
questions.expected_answer: Covalent bonding fits because the atoms share a pair of electrons.

questions.question: A student uses “sharing” and “transfer” interchangeably when labeling two bond diagrams. What distinction must they preserve to correct their labels?
questions.expected_answer: Sharing a pair describes covalent bonding. Electron transfer can create ions in an ionic example, but ionic bonding is the attraction between oppositely charged ions. Sharing and transfer must remain distinct.
